  <style>
    html,
    body {
      width: 100%;
      max-width: 100%;

      margin: 0;

      line-height: 24px;
      letter-spacing: 0px;
      color: #333
    }

    html,
    body {
      -webkit-text-size-adjust: none
    }

    * {
      border: 0;
      vertical-align: baseline;
      -webkit-box-sizing: border-box;
      -moz-box-sizing: border-box;
      box-sizing: border-box
    }

    *,
    *:hover,
    *:focus {
      outline: none !important
    }

    @media only screen and (max-width: 992px) {}

    @-webkit-keyframes BackgroundAnimation {
      from {
        -webkit-transform: translate3d(0, 0, 0);
        transform: translate3d(0, 0, 0)
      }

      to {
        -webkit-transform: translate3d(80%, 0, 0);
        transform: translate3d(80%, 0, 0)
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes BackgroundAnimationReverse {
      from {
        -webkit-transform: translate3d(0, 0, 0);
        transform: translate3d(0, 0, 0)
      }

      to {
        -webkit-transform: translate3d(-80%, 0, 0);
        transform: translate3d(-80%, 0, 0)
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes BackgroundAnimationVertical {
      from {
        -webkit-transform: translate3d(0, 0, 0);
        transform: translate3d(0, 0, 0)
      }

      to {
        -webkit-transform: translate3d(0, -70%, 0);
        transform: translate3d(0, -70%, 0)
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes itemAnimationHorizontal {
      0% {
        transform: translate(-10%, 0)
      }

      50% {
        transform: translate(10%, 0)
      }

      100% {
        transform: translate(-10%, 0)
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes itemAnimationVertical {
      0% {
        transform: translate(0, -10%)
      }

      50% {
        transform: translate(0, 10%)
      }

      100% {
        transform: translate(0, -10%)
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes itemAnimationRotate {
      0% {
        transform: rotate(-6deg)
      }

      50% {
        transform: rotate(6deg)
      }

      100% {
        transform: rotate(-6deg)
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes itemAnimationScale {
      0% {
        transform: scale(1.2)
      }

      50% {
        transform: scale(1.0)
      }

      100% {
        transform: scale(1.2)
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes animatedGradient {
      0% {
        background-position: 0% 50%
      }

      50% {
        background-position: 100% 50%
      }

      100% {
        background-position: 0% 50%
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes cssload-spin {
      100% {
        -webkit-transform: rotate(360deg);
        transform: rotate(360deg)
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes blink {
      0% {
        opacity: 1
      }

      50% {
        opacity: 0
      }

      100% {
        opacity: 1
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes clickEffect {
      100% {
        opacity: 0;
        -webkit-transform: scale(2.5)
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes drop {
      0% {
        top: 5px;
        opacity: 0
      }

      30% {
        top: 10px;
        opacity: 1
      }

      100% {
        top: 25px;
        opacity: 0
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes tabPaneChangeEffect {
      0% {
        opacity: 0;
        left: 25px
      }

      100% {
        opacity: 1;
        left: 0px
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes tabPaneChangeEffectBack {
      0% {
        opacity: 1;
        left: 0px
      }

      100% {
        opacity: 1;
        left: -25px
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes rotateplane {
      0% {
        -webkit-transform: perspective(120px)
      }

      50% {
        -webkit-transform: perspective(120px) rotateY(180deg)
      }

      100% {
        -webkit-transform: perspective(120px) rotateY(180deg) rotateX(180deg)
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes loader-signal {
      0% {
        height: 0;
        width: 0;
        background-color: #FE665C
      }

      29% {
        background-color: #FE665C
      }

      30% {
        height: 2em;
        width: 2em;
        background-color: transparent;
        border-width: 1em;
        opacity: 1
      }

      100% {
        height: 2em;
        width: 2em;
        border-width: 0;
        opacity: 0;
        background-color: transparent
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes loader-signal-label {
      0% {
        opacity: 0.25
      }

      30% {
        opacity: 1
      }

      100% {
        opacity: 0.25
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes circleRotate {
      0% {
        -webkit-transform: rotate(0deg)
      }

      100% {
        -webkit-transform: rotate(360deg)
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes sk-bouncedelay {

      0%,

      }

    @-webkit-keyframes page-loader-fade-out {

      }

        opacity: 0
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes page-loader-fade-in {
      0% {
        opacity: 0
      }

      100% {
        opacity: 1
      }
    }

<article id="post-385" class="post-385 page type-page status-publish hentry">
			<header class="page-header">
			<h1 class="page-title">SatPM2.5 (Satellite-derived PM2.5)</h1>
		</header><!-- .page-header -->
	
	<div class="page-content">
		
<figure class="wp-block-image alignright size-large is-resized"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" width="1024" height="950" src="https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2023/11/TOCb-1024x950.png" alt="" class="wp-image-1585" style="width:218px;height:201px" srcset="https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2023/11/TOCb-1024x950.png 1024w, https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2023/11/TOCb-350x325.png 350w, https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2023/11/TOCb-768x713.png 768w, https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2023/11/TOCb-1536x1426.png 1536w, https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2023/11/TOCb.png 1920w" sizes="(max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image alignleft is-resized"><img decoding="async" width="350" height="347" src="https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2023/11/ACAG-logoonly-350x347.png" alt="" class="wp-image-1580" style="width:120px;height:119px" srcset="https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2023/11/ACAG-logoonly-350x347.png 350w, https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2023/11/ACAG-logoonly-1024x1015.png 1024w, https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2023/11/ACAG-logoonly-150x150.png 150w, https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2023/11/ACAG-logoonly-768x761.png 768w, https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2023/11/ACAG-logoonly-1536x1522.png 1536w, https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2023/11/ACAG-logoonly-50x50.png 50w, https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2023/11/ACAG-logoonly.png 1920w" sizes="(max-width: 350px) 100vw, 350px" /></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Global and regional PM<sub>2.5</sub> concentrations are estimated using information from satellite-, simulation- and monitor-based sources. Aerosol optical depth from multiple satellite instruments (MODIS/Terra, MODIS/Aqua, MISR/Terra, SeaWiFS/SeaStar, VIIRS/SNPP, and VIIRS/NOAA20) and their respective retrievals (Dark Target, Deep Blue, MAIAC) is combined with simulation (GEOS-Chem) based upon their relative uncertainties as determined using ground-based sun photometer (AERONET) observations to produce geophysical estimates that explain most of the variance in ground-based PM<sub>2.5</sub> measurements. A subsequent statistical fusion incorporates additional information from PM<sub>2.5</sub> measurements.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Contents:</strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a href="#V6.GL.02.04" data-type="internal" data-id="#V6.GL.03">V6.GL.02.04</a> is recommended for users interested in our most state of the science global algorithm, and is available for 1998-2023<br><a href="#V5.GL.05.02">V5.GL.05.02</a> is also recommended for users requiring our traditional global algorithm and is available for 1998-2023<br><a href="#V5.NA.05.02">V5.NA.05/V5.NA.05.02</a> is recommended for users with a North American-only focus and includes total and compositional PM<sub>2.5</sub> for 2000-2023.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong><a href="https://forms.gle/xRqjH9VdJyy16h6bA">Registration for notification of data product updates</a></strong></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">We’ve developed a web-based tool to explore country-level PM₂.₅ data. You can access the portal at the link below:<br><a href="http://satpm25data.net">http://satpm25data.net</a></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">For a brief overview of the tool’s functionality and usage instructions, please refer to the <a href="https://wustl.box.com/s/0r5mwz7c4ey59m9nxplmuyrb6ifo33ma" data-type="page" data-id="1769" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener nofollow">instructions</a>.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Additions tools developed by users for accessing these datasets are available <a href="#TOOLS">here</a></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Previous versions are available from the <a href="https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/datasets/surface-pm2-5-archive/">SatPM<sub>2.5</sub> Archive</a></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph" id="V6.GL.02.04"><strong>Global Estimates (V6.GL.02.04):</strong></p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img decoding="async" width="884" height="402" src="https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2025/04/Screenshot-2025-04-19-at-08.02.27.png" alt="" class="wp-image-2056" srcset="https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2025/04/Screenshot-2025-04-19-at-08.02.27.png 884w, https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2025/04/Screenshot-2025-04-19-at-08.02.27-350x159.png 350w, https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2025/04/Screenshot-2025-04-19-at-08.02.27-768x349.png 768w" sizes="(max-width: 884px) 100vw, 884px" /></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">We estimate annual and monthly ground-level fine particulate matter (PM<sub>2.5</sub>) for 2000-2019 by combining Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) retrievals (Dark Target, Deep Blue, MAIAC) that make use of observations from numerous satellite-based NASA instruments (MODIS/Terra, MODIS/Aqua, MISR/Terra, SeaWiFS/SeaStar, VIIRS/SNPP, and VIIRS/NOAA20) with the GEOS-Chem chemical transport model, and subsequently calibrating to global ground-based observations using a residual Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), as detailed in the below reference for V6.GL.01. V6.GL.02.04 follows the methodology of V6.GL.01 but updates the ground-based observations used to calibrate the geophysical PM<sub>2.5</sub> estimates for the entire time series, extends temporal coverage through 1998 – 2023, and includes retrievals from the SNPP VIIRS instrument. Also, previous versions were reported to contain abnormally low values in certain, rare circumstances. This limitation has been addressed in V6.GL.02.04 using a modified padding strategy and stronger geophysical constraints.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Reference:</strong><br>Shen, S. Li, C. van Donkelaar, A. Jacobs, N. Wang, C. Martin, R. V.: <strong>Enhancing Global Estimation of Fine Particulate Matter Concentrations by Including Geophysical a Priori Information in Deep Learning. (2024) </strong>ACS ES&T Air. DOI: 10.1021/acsestair.3c00054 [<a href="https://pubs.acs.org/doi/full/10.1021/acsestair.3c00054">Link</a>]</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Note that these estimates are primarily intended to aid in large-scale studies. Annual and coarse-resolution averages correspond to a simple mean of within-grid values. Gridded datasets are provided to allow users to agglomerate data as best meets their particular needs. High-resolution (0.01° × 0.01°) datasets are gridded at the finest resolution of the information sources that were incorporated but are unlikely to fully resolve PM<sub>2.5</sub> gradients at the gridded resolution due to influence by information sources at coarser resolution.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Lijian Han (ljhan@rcees.ac.cn) has prepared an example R-based code that converts the below netcdf files to raster for import into GIS-based programs that lack netcdf support. It can be accessed via this link: <a href="https://wustl.box.com/s/9073l0k8go8kehtxd5ok46dmw1q63oav" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">[NC to Geotif.txt]</a>. Please contact Lijian if you have further questions.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">A tutorial that creates a time series of annual mean PM<sub>2.5</sub> at selected locations around the world by importing this dataset into Matlab is available <a href="https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/importing-and-plotting-the-v6-gl-02-02-dataset-into-matlab/">here</a>.</p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph">———————————————————————————</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph" id="V5.GL.05.02"><strong>Global/Regional Estimates (V5.GL.05.02):</strong></p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full is-resized"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="748" height="314" src="https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2024/12/V5GL01-F1Annual-Global-HybridPM25-202301-202312-ForRandall-ForWeb.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-1964" style="width:748px;height:314px" srcset="https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2024/12/V5GL01-F1Annual-Global-HybridPM25-202301-202312-ForRandall-ForWeb.jpg 748w, https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2024/12/V5GL01-F1Annual-Global-HybridPM25-202301-202312-ForRandall-ForWeb-350x147.jpg 350w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 748px) 100vw, 748px" /></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">We estimate annual and monthly ground-level fine particulate matter (PM<sub>2.5</sub>) for 1998-2023 by combining Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) retrievals (Dark Target, Deep Blue, and MAIAC) that use observations from multiple satellite-based NASA instruments (MODIS/Terra, MODIS/Aqua, MISR/Terra, SeaWiFS/SeaStar, VIIRS/SNPP, and VIIRS/NOAA20) with the GEOS-Chem chemical transport model (http://geos-chem.org), and subsequently calibrating to global ground-based observations using a Geographically Weighted Regression (GWR), as detailed in the below reference for V5.GL.01. V5.GL.05.02 follows the methodology of V5.GL.01, but updates the ground-based observations used to calibrate the geophysical PM<sub>2.5</sub> estimates for the entire time series, extends temporal coverage through 2023, updates satellite retrieval versions, and includes retrievals from the SNPP/NOAA VIIRS instruments.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Reference:</strong><br>Aaron van Donkelaar, Melanie S. Hammer, Liam Bindle, Michael Brauer, Jeffery R. Brook, Michael J. Garay, N. Christina Hsu, Olga V. Kalashnikova, Ralph A. Kahn, Colin Lee, Robert C. Levy, Alexei Lyapustin, Andrew M. Sayer and Randall V. Martin (2021). <strong>Monthly Global Estimates of Fine Particulate Matter and Their Uncertainty</strong> Environmental Science & Technology, 2021, doi:10.1021/acs.est.1c05309. <a href="https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/acs.est.1c05309" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">[Link]</a></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Hammer, M. S., van Donkelaar, A., Bindle, L., Sayer, A. M., Lee, J., Hsu, N. C., Levy, R.C., Sawyer, V., Garay, M. J., Kalashnikova, O. V., Kahn, R. A., Lyapustin, A., and Martin, R. V.: <strong>Assessment of the impact of discontinuity in satellite instruments and retrievals on global PM2.5 estimates</strong>. Remote Sensing of Environment, Volume 294, 2023, 113624, ISSN 0034-4257, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rse.2023.113624. [<a rel="noopener" href="https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S003442572300175X" target="_blank">Link</a>]</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Scientific Datasets:</strong><br>Annual and monthly datasets are provided in NetCDF [.nc] format. Gridded files use the WGS84 projection. Please contact Aaron van Donkelaar (aaron.vandonkelaar@wustl.edu) for further information.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Note that these estimates are primarily intended to aid in large-scale studies. Annual and coarse-resolution averages correspond to a simple mean of within-grid values. Gridded datasets are provided to allow users to agglomerate data as best meets their particular needs. High resolution (0.01° × 0.01°) datasets are gridded at the finest resolution of the information sources that were incorporated, but are unlikely to fully resolve PM<sub>2.5</sub> gradients at the gridded resolution due to influence by information sources at coarser resolution.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Lijian Han (ljhan@rcees.ac.cn) has prepared an example R-based code that converts the below netcdf files to raster for import into GIS-based programs that lack netcdf support. It can be accessed via this link: <a href="https://wustl.box.com/s/9073l0k8go8kehtxd5ok46dmw1q63oav" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">[NC to Geotif.txt]</a>. Please contact Lijian if you have further questions.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Annual and monthly mean PM<sub>2.5</sub> [ug/m<sup>3</sup>] at 0.01° × 0.01°:<br><a href="https://wustl.box.com/v/ACAG-V5GL0502-GWRPM25" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">[https://wustl.box.com/v/ACAG-V5GL0502-GWRPM25]</a><br>Annual and monthly mean PM<sub>2.5</sub> [ug/m<sup>3</sup>] at 0.1° × 0.1°:<br><a href="https://wustl.box.com/v/ACAG-V5GL0502-GWRPM25c0p05" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">[https://wustl.box.com/v/ACAG-V5GL0502-GWRPM25c0p05]</a></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Annual and monthly mean PM<sub>2.5</sub> Uncertainty [ug/m<sup>3</sup>] at 0.01° × 0.01°:<br><a href="https://wustl.box.com/v/ACAG-V5GL0502-GWRPM25SIGMA" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">[https://wustl.box.com/v/ACAG-V5GL0502-GWRPM25SIGMA]</a></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Processed Datasets:</strong><br>These summary files are processed from the Scientific Datasets above for ease of accessibility. Population-weighted estimates and total population describe only those people covered by the V5.GL.04 dataset and are provided by <a rel="noopener noreferrer" href="https://sedac.ciesin.columbia.edu/data/collection/gpw-v4" target="_blank">GPWv4</a>. Country borders are defined following <a rel="noopener noreferrer" href="https://gadm.org" target="_blank">GAD3.6</a>.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a href="https://wustl.box.com/s/zh0fzydpbfm6cqqkpgy087zv4zylxzla" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Annual Global country-level mean PM<sub>2.5</sub></a>.<br><a href="https://wustl.box.com/s/soccgzet4qjd4ro0ahwn6nliwns756id" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Annual Canada provincial-level mean PM<sub>2.5</sub></a>.<br><a href="https://wustl.box.com/s/4uljti4zll2kkgclmk628x8jwjrf5r82" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Annual China regional-level mean PM<sub>2.5</sub></a>.<br><a href="https://wustl.box.com/s/jjhtkhgti9qegvqggnej8mx62xl6wqcm" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Annual India regional-level mean PM<sub>2.5</sub></a>.<br><a href="https://wustl.box.com/s/76ce15ubblgw3wp6q8eevjglcpe67zm7" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Annual United States state-level mean PM<sub>2.5</sub></a>.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a property="dct:title" href="https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/datasets/surface-pm2-5/" rel="cc:attributionURL">SatPM<sub>2.5</sub> data V5.GL.05.02</a> are licensed under <a style="display:inline-block;" href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/?ref=chooser-v1" target="_blank" rel="license noopener noreferrer">CC BY 4.0<img decoding="async" style="height:22px!important;margin-left:3px;vertical-align:text-bottom;" src="https://mirrors.creativecommons.org/presskit/icons/cc.svg?ref=chooser-v1" alt=""><img decoding="async" style="height:22px!important;margin-left:3px;vertical-align:text-bottom;" src="https://mirrors.creativecommons.org/presskit/icons/by.svg?ref=chooser-v1" alt=""></a></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a name="V5.NA.05.02"></a><br>———————————————————————————</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>North American Regional Estimates with Composition (V5.NA.05 / V5.NA.05.02):</strong></p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-large"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1024" height="548" src="https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2023/11/V5GL01-F1-NorthAmerica-HybridPM25-2015-2015-JAN-JUL-APR-OCT-1024x548.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-1589" srcset="https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2023/11/V5GL01-F1-NorthAmerica-HybridPM25-2015-2015-JAN-JUL-APR-OCT-1024x548.jpg 1024w, https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2023/11/V5GL01-F1-NorthAmerica-HybridPM25-2015-2015-JAN-JUL-APR-OCT-350x187.jpg 350w, https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2023/11/V5GL01-F1-NorthAmerica-HybridPM25-2015-2015-JAN-JUL-APR-OCT-768x411.jpg 768w, https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2023/11/V5GL01-F1-NorthAmerica-HybridPM25-2015-2015-JAN-JUL-APR-OCT-1536x822.jpg 1536w, https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/files/2023/11/V5GL01-F1-NorthAmerica-HybridPM25-2015-2015-JAN-JUL-APR-OCT.jpg 1920w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1024px) 100vw, 1024px" /></figure>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">We estimate ground-level fine particulate matter (PM<sub>2.5</sub>) total and compositional mass concentrations over North America by combining Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) retrievals (Dark Target, Deep Blue, and MAIAC) that use observations from multiple satellite-based NASA instruments (MODIS/Terra, MODIS/Aqua, MISR/Terra, SeaWiFS/SeaStar, VIIRS/SNPP, and VIIRS/NOAA20) with the GEOS-Chem chemical transport model (http://geos-chem.org), and subsequently calibrated to regional ground-based observations of both total and compositional mass using Geographically Weighted Regression (GWR) for 2000-2023.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Reference:</strong><br>van Donkelaar, A., R. V. Martin, B. Ford, C. Li, A. J. Pappin, S. Shen, and D. Zhang, <strong>North American Fine Particulate Matter Chemical Composition for 2000–2022 from Satellites, Models, and Monitors: The Changing Contribution of Wildfires</strong>.,<em> ACS ES&T Air</em>, doi: 10.1021/acs.est.0c01764, 2024. <a href="https://pubs.acs.org/doi/full/10.1021/acsestair.4c00151" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">[Link]</a></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Scientific Datasets:</strong><br>Annual and Biweekly datasets are provided in NetCDF [.nc] or a zipped ArcGIS-compatible ASCII [.asc.zip] file. Note that the unzipped ASCII files can be cumbersome. Gridded files use the WGS84 projection.  Contact Aaron van Donkelaar (aaron.vandonkelaar@wustl.edu) for further information.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><p>Annual, monthly, and biweekly mean total PM<sub>2.5</sub> [ug/m<sup>3</sup>] at 0.01° × 0.01°: 
<br><a href="https://wustl.box.com/s/waabttesckyhpsrthwlrgu2hjcp1chqo" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">[ASCII]</a><br><a href="https://wustl.box.com/s/c3lmvqrvbjcrfpqoxb68nwl9tqhkl81g" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">[NetCDF]</a></p>
<p>Annual, monthly, and biweekly mean component PM<sub>2.5</sub> [ug/m<sup>3</sup>] at 0.01° × 0.01°: 
<br><a href="https://wustl.box.com/s/ln9ge9p7wfzrzanks9ik2kc1hwhz1g4e" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">[ASCII]</a><br><a href="https://wustl.box.com/s/i15cm0rgyjvbmwwjtomo5tmdmoyekl6g" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">[NetCDF]</a></p></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><p>The contribution of biomass burning to annual, monthly, and biweekly mean total PM<sub>2.5</sub> [ug/m<sup>3</sup>] at 0.01° × 0.01°, as described in the above publication, is additionally available from: 
<br><a href="https://wustl.box.com/s/53bcmbeip1xzt0kekll88o8adyi2xfqe" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">[ASCII]</a><br><a href="https://wustl.box.com/s/mfw4pr02b31bnp25jlwn402c93vyfjbq" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">[NetCDF]</a></p>
<p>The contribution of biomass burning to annual, monthly, and biweekly mean component PM<sub>2.5</sub> [ug/m<sup>3</sup>] at 0.01° × 0.01°, as described in the above publication, is additionally available from: 
<br><a href="https://wustl.box.com/s/gb7lr854zsm3kwyte6amg4dzjfbcqrp6" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">[ASCII]</a><br><a href="https://wustl.box.com/s/1zjqdwwcto5huijiluk26qyrmzazhe29" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">[NetCDF]</a></p></p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Note that these estimates are primarily intended to aid in large-scale studies. Gridded datasets are provided to allow users to agglomerate data as best meets their particular needs. Datasets are gridded at the finest resolution of the information sources that were incorporated (0.01° × 0.01°), but do not fully resolve PM<sub>2.5</sub> gradients at the gridded resolution due to influence by information sources at coarser resolution.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><a name="TOOLS"></a><br>———————————————————————————<br>We sincerely appreciate the efforts by our users to develop tools that facilitate access of our PM<sub>2.5</sub> estimates. While we don’t directly service these codes, we gratefully make them available for others to use. Please contact the developer indicated if you have any questions.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">– Lijian Han (ljhan@rcees.ac.cn) has prepared an example R-based code that converts the netcdf files we provide into raster for import into GIS-based programs that lack netcdf support. It can be accessed via this link: <a href="https://wustl.box.com/s/9073l0k8go8kehtxd5ok46dmw1q63oav" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">[NC to Geotif.txt]</a>.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">– MITRE’s Health Equity MIP has developed an open-source R package for particulate matter 2.5 data called <a href="https://github.com/mitre/acagpm" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">[ACAGPM]</a>. This package aligns ACAG’s particulate matter 2.5 data with 2019 census geographies, allowing users to efficiently analyze PM<sub>2.5</sub> as it relates to social determinants of health and other variables. For more information, please reach out to the lead contributors indicated via github.</p>

      from {
        -webkit-transform: translate3d(0, 0, 0);

      }

      to {
        -webkit-transform: translate3d(80%, 0, 0);
        transform: translate3d(80%, 0, 0)
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes BackgroundAnimationReverse {
      from {
        -webkit-transform: translate3d(0, 0, 0);
        transform: translate3d(0, 0, 0)
      }

      to {
        -webkit-transform: translate3d(-80%, 0, 0);
        transform: translate3d(-80%, 0, 0)
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes BackgroundAnimationVertical {
      from {
        -webkit-transform: translate3d(0, 0, 0);
        transform: translate3d(0, 0, 0)
      }

      to {
        -webkit-transform: translate3d(0, -70%, 0);
        transform: translate3d(0, -70%, 0)
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes itemAnimationHorizontal {
      0% {
        transform: translate(-10%, 0)
      }

        transform: translate(10%, 0)
      }

        transform: translate(-10%, 0)
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes itemAnimationVertical {
      0% {
        transform: translate(0, -10%)
      }

      50% {
        transform: translate(0, 10%)
      }

      100% {
        transform: translate(0, -10%)
      }
    }

    @-webkit-keyframes itemAnimationRotate {
      0% {
        transform: rotate(-6deg)
      }

      50% {
        transform: rotate(6deg)
      }

      100% {
        transform: rotate(-6deg)
      }
    }

      0% {

        transform: scale(1.0)
      }

        transform: scale(1.2)
      }

      }

        background-position: 0% 50%
      }

Registry of Open Data on AWS

About

This registry exists to help people discover and share datasets that are available via AWS resources. See recent additions and learn more about sharing data on AWS.

Get started using data quickly by viewing all tutorials with associated SageMaker Studio Lab notebooks.

See all usage examples for datasets listed in this registry.

See datasets from EPA, Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence (AI2), Allen Institute, Biohub, Digital Earth Africa, Data for Good at Meta, NASA Space Act Agreement, NIH STRIDES, NOAA Open Data Dissemination Program, Space Telescope Science Institute, and Amazon Sustainability Data Initiative.

Search datasets (currently 13 matching datasets)

Add to this registry

If you want to add a dataset or example of how to use a dataset to this registry, please follow the instructions on the Registry of Open Data on AWS GitHub repository.

Unless specifically stated in the applicable dataset documentation, datasets available through the Registry of Open Data on AWS are not provided and maintained by AWS. Datasets are provided and maintained by a variety of third parties under a variety of licenses. Please check dataset licenses and related documentation to determine if a dataset may be used for your application.

Tell us about your project

If you have a project using a listed dataset, please tell us about it. We may work with you to feature your project in a blog post.

The Human Sleep Project

bioinformaticsdeep learninglife sciencesmachine learningmedicineneurophysiologyneuroscience

The Human Sleep Project (HSP) sleep physiology dataset is a growing collection of clinical polysomnography (PSG) recordings. Beginning with PSG recordings from from ~15K patients evaluated at the Massachusetts General Hospital, the HSP will grow over the coming years to include data from >200K patients, as well as people evaluated outside of the clinical setting. This data is being used to develop CAISR (Complete AI Sleep Report), a collection of deep neural networks, rule-based algorithms, and signal processing approaches designed to provide better-than-human detection of conventional PSG...

It is a key component of blue water fluxes in water accounting. Blue ET consists of evaporation from irrigated fields, transpiration from irrigated crops, and water lost from artificial storage. It helps assess water productivity in irrigated agriculture, quantify consumptive water use, and support sustainable water resource management, particularly in water-scarce regions.

artifacts.content:
=== PDF page 2 ===
                                       -2-



              4.   Peraturan Presiden Nomor 16 Tahun 2015 tentang
                   Kementerian        Lingkungan          Hidup     dan    Kehutanan
                   (Lembaran        Negara     Republik    Indonesia      Tahun   2015
                   Nomor 17);
              5.   Peraturan Menteri Lingkungan Hidup dan Kehutanan
                   Nomor P.18/MENLHK-II/2015 tentang Organisasi dan
                   Tata     Kerja     Kementerian         Lingkungan      Hidup    dan
                   Kehutanan         (Berita      Negara      Republik       Indonesia
                   Tahun 2015 Nomor 713);


                               MEMUTUSKAN:
Menetapkan   : PERATURAN        MENTERI           LINGKUNGAN           HIDUP       DAN
              KEHUTANAN        TENTANG          INDEKS      STANDAR        PENCEMAR
              UDARA.


                                                Pasal 1
              Dalam Peraturan Menteri ini yang dimaksud dengan:
              1.   Indeks    Standar     Pencemar         Udara    yang    selanjutnya
                   disingkat ISPU adalah angka yang tidak mempunyai
                   satuan    yang      menggambarkan         kondisi      mutu    udara
                   ambien di lokasi tertentu, yang didasarkan kepada
                   dampak terhadap kesehatan manusia, nilai estetika dan
                   makhluk hidup lainnya.
              2.   Stasiun     Pemantau         Kualitas    Udara      Ambien      yang
                   selanjutnya disingkat SPKUA adalah perangkat yang
                   terdiri atas peralatan pemantau kualitas udara ambien
                   yang beroperasi secara terus-menerus dan datanya dapat
                   dipantau secara langsung.
              3.   Perangkat        Pengolah     Data     adalah    perangkat      yang
                   digunakan         untuk       menerima,         menghitung      dan
                   menyimpan data hasil pemantauan.
              4.   Status Warna adalah indikator kondisi masing-masing
                   kategori rentang ISPU.
              5.   Menteri adalah menteri yang menyelenggarakan urusan
                   pemerintahan di bidang perlindungan dan pengelolaan
                   lingkungan hidup.

=== PDF page 3 ===
                        -3-



                                 Pasal 2
(1)   Menteri, gubernur, dan bupati/wali kota bertanggung
      jawab dalam menentukan ISPU.
(2)   ISPU sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) meliputi
      parameter:
      a.   partikulat (PM10);
      b.   partikulat (PM2.5);
      c.   karbon monoksida (CO);
      d.   nitrogen dioksida (NO2);
      e.   sulfur dioksida (SO2);
      f.   ozon (O3); dan
      g.   hidrokarbon (HC).
(3)   ISPU sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1) ditentukan
      dengan tahapan:
      a.   perhitungan;
      b.   pelaporan; dan
      c.   publikasi.


                                 Pasal 3
Perhitungan ISPU sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 2
ayat (3) huruf a dilakukan melalui kegiatan:
a.    pemantauan; dan
b.    konversi konsentrasi parameter menjadi nilai ISPU.


                                 Pasal 4
(1)   Pemantauan sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 3
      huruf a harus memenuhi persyaratan:
      a.   peralatan SPKUA; dan
      b.   lokasi pemantauan.
(2)   Persyaratan peralatan SPKUA sebagaimana dimaksud
      pada ayat (1) huruf a meliputi:
      a.   alat pemantau kualitas udara;
      b.   alat pemantau meteorologi;
      c.   Perangkat Pengolah Data; dan
      d.   beroperasi selama 24 (dua puluh empat) jam secara
           terus-menerus.

=== PDF page 4 ===
                           -4-



(3)   Persyaratan lokasi pemantauan sebagaimana dimaksud
      pada ayat (1) huruf b meliputi:
      a.   klasifikasi lokasi pemantauan, yang meliputi:
           1.    pusat kota;
           2.    latar kota;
           3.    sub-urban;
           4.    industri;
           5.    pedesaan; dan
           6.    lokasi lainnya yang mengarah kepada sumber
                 pencemar tertentu,
           dan
      b.   kriteria       penempatan        peralatan     SPKUA,         yang
           meliputi:
           1.     ditempatkan pada udara terbuka dengan sudut
                  terbuka      120°   (seratus    dua     puluh       derajat)
                  terhadap penghalang;
           2.     ketinggian      sampling     inlet    dari    permukaan
                  tanah untuk partikel dan gas paling sedikit 2
                  (dua) meter; dan
           3.     jarak    alat   pemantau       kualitas       udara    dari
                  sumber emisi terdekat paling sedikit 20 (dua
                  puluh) meter.


                                  Pasal 5
(1)   Pemantauan sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 3
      huruf a dilakukan secara terus-menerus.
(2)   Hasil pemantauan berupa:
      a.   data     konsentrasi       udara      ambien        pada     setiap
           parameter sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 2
           ayat (2); dan
      b.   data meteorologi yang mempengaruhi konsentrasi
           udara      ambien       sebagaimana         dimaksud         dalam
           huruf a.
(3)   Data meteorologi sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (2)
      huruf b meliputi:
      a.   kecepatan dan arah angin;
      b.   temperatur udara;

=== PDF page 5 ===
                       -5-



      c.   kelembaban;
      d.   intensitas matahari; dan/atau
      e.   curah hujan.
(4)   Data hasil pemantauan sebagaimana dimaksud pada
      ayat (2) digunakan sebagai dasar konversi konsentrasi
      parameter menjadi nilai ISPU.


                                 Pasal 6
(1)   Perhitungan ISPU sebagaimana dimaksud dalam Pasal 4
      dan Pasal 5 dilakukan setiap 1 (satu) jam dari data
      pemantauan 24 (dua puluh empat) jam secara terus-
      menerus.
(2)   Perhitungan ISPU dilakukan berdasarkan nilai:
      a.   ISPU batas atas;
      b.   ISPU batas bawah;
      c.   ambien batas atas;
      d.   ambien batas bawah; dan
      e.   konsentrasi ambien hasil pengukuran.
(3)   Tata cara perhitungan ISPU sebagaimana tercantum
      dalam   Lampiran       I   yang      merupakan     bagian     tidak
      terpisahkan dari Peraturan Menteri ini.


                                 Pasal 7
(1)   Terhadap hasil perhitungan ISPU sebagaimana dimaksud
      dalam Pasal 6 dilakukan penjaminan mutu melalui:
      a.   pemeriksaan kelengkapan data harian konsentrasi
           setiap paramater sebagaimana dimaksud dalam
           Pasal 3 ayat (1); dan
      b.   penghapusan       data    yang     tidak    normal     dengan
           menggunakan sistem aplikasi validasi data.
(2)   Penghapusan data sebagaimana dimaksud pada ayat (1)
      huruf b dilakukan dalam hal:
      a.   sedang dilakukan pemeliharaan SPKUA;
      b.   ketidakstabilan       tegangan    listrik   pada     peralatan
           SPKUA;
      c.   adanya gangguan pada sensor; atau
      d.   terjadi pemadaman listrik.

=== PDF page 7 ===
                          -7-



                                  Pasal 9
(1)   Menteri, gubernur, dan bupati/wali kota menyusun
      laporan hasil penentuan kategori ISPU berdasarkan
      masing-masing SPKUA.
(2)   Laporan hasil penentuan kategori ISPU sebagaimana
      dimaksud pada ayat (1) harus dilengkapi dengan data
      dan informasi:
      a.     waktu pelaporan;
      b.     waktu pengukuran;
      c.     lokasi yang dilaporkan;
      d.     keterangan     lokasi         pemantauan        sebagaimana
             dimaksud dalam Pasal 4 ayat (3) huruf a;
      e.     parameter pencemar kritis;
      f.     ISPU paling tinggi;
      g.     kategori ISPU; dan
      h.     konsentrasi.
(3)   Laporan hasil penentuan kategori ISPU sebagaimana
      dimaksud      pada    ayat     (2)    diintegrasikan    ke   laman
      http://iku.menlhk.go.id/aqms/.
(4)   Pengintegrasian sistem ISPU sebagaimana dimaksud
      pada ayat (3) dikoordinasikan oleh Direktur Jenderal
      yang     membidangi        urusan     pengendalian     pencemaran
      udara.


                                Pasal 10
(1)   Menteri, gubernur dan bupati/wali kota menyediakan
      informasi publik mengenai hasil penentuan kategori
      ISPU:
      a.     setiap jam selama 24 (dua puluh empat) jam untuk
             parameter partikulat (PM2,5); dan
      b.     paling sedikit 2 (dua) kali dalam 1 (satu) hari untuk
             parameter partikulat (PM10), sulfur dioksida (SO2),
             karbon monoksida (CO), ozon (O3), nitrogen dioksida
             (NO2) dan hidrokarbon (HC).
(2)   Dalam hal ISPU berada pada kategori tidak sehat, sangat
      tidak sehat, atau berbahaya, Menteri, gubernur dan
      bupati/wali kota menyediakan informasi publik mengenai

                                                Pasal 1
              Dalam Peraturan Menteri ini yang dimaksud dengan:
              1.   Indeks    Standar     Pencemar         Udara    yang    selanjutnya
                   disingkat ISPU adalah angka yang tidak mempunyai
                   satuan    yang      menggambarkan         kondisi      mutu    udara
                   ambien di lokasi tertentu, yang didasarkan kepada
                   dampak terhadap kesehatan manusia, nilai estetika dan
                   makhluk hidup lainnya.
              2.   Stasiun     Pemantau         Kualitas    Udara      Ambien      yang
                   selanjutnya disingkat SPKUA adalah perangkat yang
                   terdiri atas peralatan pemantau kualitas udara ambien
                   yang beroperasi secara terus-menerus dan datanya dapat
                   dipantau secara langsung.
              3.   Perangkat        Pengolah     Data     adalah    perangkat      yang
                   digunakan         untuk       menerima,         menghitung      dan
                   menyimpan data hasil pemantauan.
              4.   Status Warna adalah indikator kondisi masing-masing
                   kategori rentang ISPU.
              5.   Menteri adalah menteri yang menyelenggarakan urusan
                   pemerintahan di bidang perlindungan dan pengelolaan
                   lingkungan hidup.
findings.timeBasis: Article 6: calculated hourly from continuous 24-hour monitoring. Article 10: PM2.5 published hourly; other parameters at least twice daily. These are not annual means.
findings.pollutantChoice: Annex I example reports the maximum pollutant ISPU and critical pollutant. A high value need not mean PM2.5 is the critical pollutant.
findings.indexDistinction: ISPU is a station-based short-term index. Administrative IKU is separate and belongs to the parent index audit; no IKU panel duplicated.
findings.qualityControl: Article 7 requires daily concentration completeness checks and deletion of abnormal observations during maintenance, unstable voltage, sensor faults or power outages. These rules alone do not certify actual 2023 completeness.

investigations.name: ACAG V6.GL.02.04 satellite/model/monitor-fused annual PM2.5
investigations.concept: Retrospective modelled annual near-surface PM2.5 concentration; not a ground-station observation or administrative index
investigations.publisher: Atmospheric Composition Analysis Group, Washington University in St. Louis

recommendation.reason: A credible 2023 annual Asia raster is verified in the provider listing, but no 27-district estimates or required aggregation evidence are available in this bundle.

findings.method: Satellite aerosol optical depth plus GEOS-Chem geophysical estimates, calibrated to global ground observations using a residual convolutional neural network. The provider says calibration updates affect the entire time series.
findings.yearSelection: Annual Asia filename explicitly 202301–202312; not a monthly layer, 2022 substitute, national summary or current forecast.
findings.downloadEvidence: Folder metadata identifies a 90,942,270-byte NetCDF file. Raster bytes were not downloaded or evaluated; file size is metadata, not a hash or observed grid contents.
findings.sourceVintage: Provider describes 2024 method publication and updated 1998–2023 series; listed 2023 Asia file was created/updated at Unix timestamp 1750825087 (2025-06-25 UTC). Record version explicitly, not as data available in 2023.
findings.licence: Provider page states CC BY 4.0 for V6.GL.02.04.
findings.limitations: Provider warns these estimates primarily support large-scale studies. Annual and coarse averages are simple means of within-grid values. Fine grid spacing does not fully resolve concentration gradients because some input information is coarser.
findings.processedPanels: Accessed provider page lists country summaries and subnational summaries for Canada, China, India and the United States; it does not list Indonesian kabupaten/kota estimates.
findings.aggregationDecision: Do not sample one centroid or copy a country value into 27 regions. A modelled district panel requires an explicit boundary vintage, area/population estimand, valid-cell coverage and reproducible zonal aggregation.
findings.failedAlternativeMirror: The linked AWS registry URL returned HTTP 404 with a large registry page, not this model dataset. Box source listings were then fetched successfully.

gaps: No approved 2023 kabupaten/kota boundaries and spatial crosswalk applied to the raster.
No district raster cell intersection, land mask, valid-area coverage or uncertainty assessment performed.
No agreed area-weighted environmental-state versus population-weighted exposure estimand; population weights would require their own documented vintage and coverage.
No 27-row district panel published in the accessed provider listings; the model is an available annual grid, not a district observation table.
High-resolution gridding does not establish effective 0.01-degree accuracy or full resolution of within-district gradients.
Scientific algorithm and calibration are retrospective; a 2023 reference year does not imply a 2023 publication vintage.

coverageDecision.decision: No air exposure candidate meets affirmative evidence for a 2023 annual all-27-region panel. This is an evidence decision, not a claim that every source lacks data.
coverageDecision.preservedNumericContext: Three official annual 2023 SPM/TSP station summaries are preserved inside the investigation, not promoted to district observations. Current 2026 station rows remain raw access evidence only.
coverageDecision.modelAvailability: A specific 2023 annual Asia PM2.5 NetCDF is listed by the provider; district extraction and representativeness gates are not met.
coverageDecision.missingness: No zero imputation, interpolation, other-year substitution, centroid district proxy or invented district value. No numeric district series emitted.
coverageDecision.recommendedUse: Keep SPM station context and current monitoring footprint as context only. Park annual PM2.5/PM10, ISPU and modelled district candidates until year, coverage, aggregation and source-vintage evidence are established.

accessNotes.searchEvidence: Search snippets guided discovery only; no numeric value relies on search snippets.
accessNotes.failedFetches: Retained exact direct HTTP error bodies as diagnostics. A direct 403 and successful native-reader extraction are separate access methods, not contradictory data observations.
accessNotes.sourceRestriction: Only relevant exact page text is retained for the BPS publication, with full PDF hash and byte count; no complete book redistributed.
accessNotes.methodScope: Bounded official monitoring, one official statistical publication and one established academic model-provider family; no expansive literature chase.
accessNotes.verification: No build, lint, tests, formatter or production execution performed.
